author: 𝑺𝒕✩𝒓𝒈𝒊𝒓𝒍 | CELEBRITY ASTROLOGER
text: the younger crowd on tiktok is saying they struggle with journaling because they don’t know how to do it without being performative for anyone/their future self reading it … there’s genuinely no hope for the psychological damage that existing solely to be observed has inflicted

topReplies.author: Briar
topReplies.text: Not just the younger kids, I've always felt like this. Even when thinking to myself... though I have always felt like there were hidden cameras watching me, even in my house, and that maybe someone was hearing my thoughts... so there might be more going on there

topReplies.author: Jayde ₊˚⊹ ᰔ
topReplies.text: Personally I think we should be performative for ourselves. I want to impress future me actually
honestly i think the cure for them is learning how to be sentimental. they’re all afraid of corniness or being vulnerable. they think detachment saves them from the fate we all have to face.

topReplies.author: shereen
topReplies.text: even when I was (very sparingly) writing diary entries as a kid ~2005, I imagined my future self reading them or my parents finding them, and def wrote in a way that suggested an audience. maybe these kids are actually more self-aware of that than I was but just have to let it go

topReplies.author: hannie'bobannie
topReplies.text: I was struggling with Journaling at first because of this, but then I really just said fuck it and started writing my wildest thoughts and emotions without any regard to grammar or spelling and now I journal all the time. You have to let go, thats the point of Journaling.

topReplies.author: Thoughts & Tidbits
topReplies.text:
It’s honestly so sad, I understand the fear of what if someone else reads all your thoughts, but there are ways around it

When I first started journaling with that same fear, I would write and then just throw the pages away

topReplies.author: James
topReplies.text: I seriously struggle to bring myself to draw or engage with any activity where you naturally start as a beginner bc even if I’m alone I fear being judged too much and disappoint myself easily bc my standards are too high. Been trying to unlearn this but it’s not easy

topReplies.author: amande
topReplies.text: Hmm what's so bad about being a bit performative though? I'm sure it holds for anyone that if you've never journaled before, your first X entries will be quite performative.

topReplies.author: FutureIntact
topReplies.text: This is concerning but it takes practice. I've gone through various phases in how I approach journaling. It's a kind of superpower for consciousness and can be used for good or bad. Only in my 40s was I able to journal for an entire month straight without missing a day.Keep at it

topReplies.author: noël ‹𝟹
topReplies.text: This is very normal actually let’s not shame children / teens for something that is literally not new or specific to them lol

topReplies.author: granddaughter
topReplies.text: nooo they just need time & often different surroundings. the world is different now, absolutely. yet it’s a world created for them and they’ll definitely find their way as we all do with the passage of time.

topReplies.author: caitie
topReplies.text: i struggle with journaling because one time i wrote my biggest insecurities in my journal which my brother then read and proceeded to tease me over. suffice to say i never wrote anything like that down again

topReplies.author: Jobo
topReplies.text: Can’t make people do what they don’t want to do. The first step imo would be not to shame them for it. There’s always a reason for why people do things. Don’t skip to dismissing their worth without considering their story.

topReplies.author: chloe
topReplies.text: this isnt a new thing. if I remember correctly, a lot of journals written throughout history were made with that exact thought in mind

topReplies.author: afflicted with whosteria
topReplies.text: You have to throw the journal entry out afterward. Makes a world of difference.
